investor_qa.quote: We continue to assess our disclosure practices in alignment with our mission and policies and in response to shareholder feedback, and are considering possible enhancements, including more disclosure in certain expense categories.

value.topic: PitchBook pricing philosophy
value.stated_position: Pricing philosophy is "simple, all-inclusive pricing"; management prioritizes growing with clients over steeper short-term price increases, and expects significant revenue growth from continuing to move firms onto firmwide (enterprise) licenses.

investor_qa.quote: At the same time, we put a high priority on ensuring that we can grow with our clients, which shows up in renewal rates and an increased user base and, we believe, creates more value in the long term than might be offered by steeper, short-term increases in price.

value.topic: LCD integration and transition of clients off the legacy product
value.stated_position: With the LCD integration substantially complete, the focus is on moving clients off the legacy LCD product onto the PitchBook platform, on track to be fully complete by the end of the year.

investor_qa.quote: With the substantial completion of the LCD integration, LCD news, data, and research is available on the PitchBook platform, and we are now focused on moving clients off the legacy LCD product and onto the PitchBook platform. PitchBook is on track to fully complete this transition by the end of the year.

value.topic: LCD acquisition outcome and pricing decision post-acquisition
value.stated_position: Management said it deliberately did not raise pricing as much as it might have following LCD, focusing instead on introducing both client groups to the broader data sets; and acknowledged limited client overlap resulted in "a small amount of expected customer leakage."

investor_qa.quote: Specific to the LCD transaction and integration, we did not increase pricing as much as we might have been able given the expanded data and research available to both legacy LCD and PitchBook clients following the acquisition.

value.topic: PitchBook long-term margin potential and reinvestment tradeoff
value.stated_position: Management believes PitchBook can approach Data and Analytics margins over time but remains focused on the long term and balancing investment in data, research, and platform capabilities against a significant global market opportunity.

investor_qa.quote: While we think PitchBook can approach Data and Analytics margins over time, we remain focused on the long term and continuing to balance the right level of investment in data, research, and platform capabilities to capitalize on what we still believe is a significant global market opportunity.

value.topic: PitchBook leadership transition from John Gabbert to Rod Diefendorf
value.stated_position: Management said strategic plans are designed so that "a leadership transition alone does not lead to a strategy change," anticipating no material changes in strategy or prioritization; Rod, PitchBook's COO since 2016, provides "stability and continuity."

investor_qa.quote: One of the key goals of our strategic planning process is that the resulting plans should be durable and long-term oriented. This means that our goal is to ensure that a leadership transition alone does not lead to a strategy change. In that vein, we anticipate no material changes in strategy or prioritization with Rod stepping in to lead PitchBook.

value.topic: PitchBook strategic priorities under new leadership
value.stated_position: Central strategy is to lead in all areas of private market data and research by expanding breadth and depth of data, including global coverage in APAC and emerging markets, and building unique analytics, IP and market intelligence.

investor_qa.quote: Central to that strategy is to lead in all areas of private market data and research by continually expanding the breadth and depth of our data and product capabilities to meet evolving private market investor needs. Current priorities in support of that strategy include continuing to expand our coverage of private companies, credit, and funds, in part through bolstering our global coverage, most notably in APAC and emerging markets.

value.topic: PitchBook management bonus plan following Gabbert departure
value.stated_position: John was the primary beneficiary of the PitchBook management bonus plan, forfeited his unvested shares on departure, and the company plans to terminate the plan.

investor_qa.quote: John was the primary beneficiary of the PitchBook management bonus plan, and, with his departure he forfeited his unvested shares. With his departure and Rod's promotion to President of PitchBook we are planning to terminate the plan.

value.topic: Morningstar Credit competitive position vs larger rating agencies
value.stated_position: Management sees opportunity for mid-sized credit rating agencies such as Morningstar DBRS to gain market coverage in private credit and esoteric ABS, where it believes it competes better than in public corporate bond markets.

investor_qa.quote: Despite the first quarter trend, we continue to see opportunity for mid-sized credit rating agencies such as Morningstar DBRS to gain market coverage, with good growth opportunities in areas including private credit and esoteric asset-backed securities, where we believe we're better able to compete with the larger credit agencies compared to the public corporate bond markets with its prevailing index eligibility guidelines.

value.topic: Reinvestment in Morningstar Credit capacity
value.stated_position: Management said it is prudently reinvesting to support future growth, particularly in Europe and the U.S. with a focus on corporates and structured finance, building capacity to expand coverage and capabilities.

investor_qa.quote: Importantly, we are prudently reinvesting in some areas to support future growth, particularly in Europe and the U.S. with a focus on corporates and areas of structured finance. Here, we are building capacity to expand coverage and capabilities.

value.topic: Real estate footprint and capital expenditures
value.stated_position: Management expects capex headwinds from future real estate decisions as it consolidates certain locations, including Canada, New York, and Mumbai, reducing rent but requiring capital to remodel or refit.

investor_qa.quote: As we look to optimize our real estate footprint, we are consolidating certain locations which will reduce rent but require capital to remodel or refit new or existing locations. We expect this activity will include some of our larger markets including Canada, New York, and Mumbai.

value.topic: Disclosure of financial impact of the AssetMark strategic alliance
value.stated_position: Management pointed to the updated Investor FAQ for context on the expected financial impact and said: "Beyond this, we are not disclosing further details related to the transaction, including the exact anticipated impact on operating expense or operating income from the transaction."

investor_qa.quote: Beyond this, we are not disclosing further details related to the transaction, including the exact anticipated impact on operating expense or operating income from the transaction.

value.topic: Relative size of the seven primary customer groups
value.stated_position: Management declined to give revenue percentages but ranked its five largest customer groups by annual contract value through June 2024, from largest to smallest: private market investors; advisors and wealth managers; asset managers; fixed-income security issuers and arrangers; retirement market participants. value.topic: Further M&A in private markets, and whether Preqin would have complemented PitchBook
value.stated_position: Management said that while Preqin is a competitor to PitchBook, "we did not see its capabilities as additive to the PitchBook platform," claimed competitiveness on fund and benchmark data and a "market-leading position" in broader global private market coverage, and reiterated that reduced leverage "alone is not a catalyst for M&A." It remains "opportunistic" subject to strategic objectives and IRR hurdles, but "our focus right now is on organic growth opportunities across the business."

investor_qa.quote: As we discussed in more detail in a May 2024 response to a related question, while the recent reduction in leverage gives us flexibility, that alone is not a catalyst for M&A. That said, our focus right now is on organic growth opportunities across the business, and we are confident in our ability to drive sustainable growth and value creation with our current portfolio and markets that we serve.

value.topic: Long-term decline in Morningstar.com US memberships since 2007
value.stated_position: Management acknowledged memberships "peaked at roughly 180,000 in December 2007 and declined to roughly 100,000 by December 2023," attributing the decline to the aftermath of the global financial crisis, the move toward passive investing shifting focus from investment selection, increased competition from other financial websites and online brokerage platforms "many of whom license our data and research to fuel their offerings," and price increases (prices up more than 50% since 2007). It said that since late 2023 it has "started to see early signs of an encouraging trend in subscriptions, driven in part by our strategic focus on search engine marketing and enhanced targeting programs."

investor_qa.quote: Memberships peaked at roughly 180,000 in December 2007 and declined to roughly 100,000 by December 2023. The decline over this time period can be traced to several factors.

value.topic: Trade-off between revenue growth and margin expansion at PitchBook
value.stated_position: Management says it focuses on maximizing long-term value creation, sees "meaningful opportunity for additional growth and steady margin expansion" at PitchBook, monitors SaaS metrics such as customer acquisition costs and customer lifetime value, and does not believe it faces a binary choice between revenue and margin growth today.

investor_qa.quote: In balancing revenue growth and margin expansion across the business, we focus on maximizing long-term value creation. In the case of PitchBook specifically, we see meaningful opportunity for additional growth and steady margin expansion.

value.topic: Whether another large investment cycle should be expected; margin volatility
value.stated_position: Management acknowledges recent margin volatility came from investments in Morningstar Wealth and Morningstar Sustainalytics plus market headwinds, and says growth ahead is expected to be "largely self-funded," i.e. revenues increasing faster than expenses with increasing adjusted operating margins over time.

investor_qa.quote: As we look across our segments, we believe that we have good opportunities for organic growth and, as we noted at the annual shareholders meeting, we expect that growth to be largely self-funded. That means we are focused on increasing revenues at a faster rate than expenses with increasing adjusted operating margins over time.

value.topic: Termination of the PitchBook management bonus plan following the founder's departure
value.stated_position: Following the departure of John Gabbert, PitchBook's founder and former CEO, the company terminated the PitchBook management bonus plan in Q3 24, stating the plan "was designed primarily as a compensation vehicle for John," and that its termination eliminates an important driver of volatility in PitchBook's adjusted operating margins.

investor_qa.quote: Following the departure of John Gabbert, PitchBook’s founder and former CEO, we terminated the PitchBook management bonus plan in Q3 24. The plan was designed primarily as a compensation vehicle for John.

value.topic: Weak corporate client segment at PitchBook and change in sales approach
value.stated_position: Management says it has reevaluated sales and customer support strategies for corporates with limited use cases and higher churn, so PitchBook can prioritize prospects and clients with stronger use cases and higher customer lifetime value.

investor_qa.quote: Given the softness in new sales and client retention within the client segment, we’ve reevaluated sales and customer support strategies for corporates with limited use cases who tend to have higher churn over time and lower lifetime customer value. This will allow PitchBook to prioritize prospects and clients with stronger use cases and the potential for higher customer lifetime value.

value.topic: Competitive position versus Preqin after BlackRock's acquisition
value.stated_position: Management claims PitchBook is "the market leader in private market data based on the breadth and depth of our coverage," says coverage of private fund and benchmark data is comparable to Preqin's, declines to comment on BlackRock's plans, and says it remains focused on its long-term strategy and intensely focused on servicing customers as a core competitive advantage.

investor_qa.quote: While we’re not in a position to comment on BlackRock’s plans for Preqin, we remain focused on our long-term strategy for PitchBook of delivering value to customers and continue to see a strong runway for growth.

value.topic: "Rule of 40" and PitchBook profitability discipline
value.stated_position: Management agrees it is necessary to strike a balance between revenue growth and profitability to generate long-term value for shareholders, declines to disclose incremental margins, and says it is committed to balancing the right level of investment in data, research, and platform capabilities.

investor_qa.quote: We are committed to balancing the right level of investment in data, research, and platform capabilities to capitalize on what we still believe is a significant global market opportunity.

value.topic: Investment plans and market-share ambition for Morningstar Credit
value.stated_position: Management says it did not make significant investments in H1 24 and headcount was lower, but in H2 24 it is adding analyst capacity in private and middle market credit, "esoteric" asset-backed securities, project finance and infrastructure; and as a challenger to incumbents it sees opportunity for continued growth and margin expansion over time.

investor_qa.quote: In H2 24, we are adding analyst capacity in a few key targeted areas including private and middle market credit and “esoteric” asset-backed securities, as well as project finance and infrastructure.

value.topic: Approach to credit market cyclicality
value.stated_position: Management says it is difficult to provide a "normalized" growth rate given cyclicality and rate sensitivity, and states the aim is to grow market share regardless of the environment.

investor_qa.quote: Given the cyclicality and sensitivity of credit markets to the interest rate and spread environment, it’s difficult to provide a “normalized” growth rate. Our aim is to grow market share regardless of the environment.

value.topic: De-emphasis of the exchange market data "broadcast feed" product
value.stated_position: Management states it has been less focused on the broadcast feed product because it does not align as well with Morningstar's other core data sets.

investor_qa.quote: Meanwhile, exchange market data performance reflected softness especially in our “broadcast feed” product. We have not been as focused on this product given that it does not align as well with our other core data sets.

value.topic: Competitors in managed investment, market and equity data
value.stated_position: Management names FE fundinfo and LSEG (Refinitiv) as main global competitors for managed investment data, plus smaller local/regional players, and Bloomberg, FactSet, ICE Data Services, LSEG (Refinitiv), and S&P Global for market and equity data.

investor_qa.quote: Our main global competitors for managed investment data, including mutual fund data, include FE fundinfo and LSEG (Refinitiv). We also compete against smaller players that focus on local or regional information. For market and equity data, we primarily compete with Bloomberg, FactSet, ICE Data Services, LSEG (Refinitiv), and S&P Global.

value.topic: Morningstar Retirement margin ceiling and growth outlook
value.stated_position: Management describes margins as reflecting successful scaling of the business and distribution model built with recordkeepers since 2000/2003, and says while there are future margin opportunities, "they are not as meaningful as the potential expansion in other parts of our business."

investor_qa.quote: While we also have future opportunities for margin growth in Morningstar Retirement, they are not as meaningful as the potential expansion in other parts of our business.

value.topic: Near-term priorities for Morningstar Sustainalytics
value.stated_position: Management highlights three near-term priorities: climate (regulatory/reporting use cases and banking clients), broader data set improvements including CSRD support, and strengthening the second-party opinion product and leveraging it in investor solutions, especially for banks exploring transition financing.

investor_qa.quote: Finally, we are committed to strengthening our market-leading second party-opinion product (SPOs) and finding opportunities to leverage our strength there in investor solutions, especially in supporting banks exploring transition-financing investment opportunities.

value.topic: Sustainalytics differentiation versus MSCI and other ESG providers
value.stated_position: Management says the key differentiator is connecting ESG data and analytics strengths with capabilities elsewhere in Morningstar, notes it is one of the leading providers of ESG data, and says it is "winning some deals and losing others" with no strong directional trend in market share.

investor_qa.quote: In general, it’s our observation that we’re winning some deals and losing others, but we haven’t seen a strong trend in one direction to suggest our market share has changed materially.

value.topic: Winding down the bespoke on-demand licensed ratings product in corporate solutions
value.stated_position: Management says it concluded the bespoke, on-demand ratings product was not scalable, is winding it down, and is instead focusing on licensing existing ratings, underlying data, benchmarking and tools to corporates — a strategy it believes it can scale successfully over time.

investor_qa.quote: Historically, we offered a bespoke, on-demand ratings product that we ultimately concluded was not scalable. We’re winding down that offering and instead focusing on licensing the use and distribution of existing ratings and underlying data, benchmarking, and tools to corporates to help them make decisions, compare themselves to peers, and use in marketing materials.

value.topic: "Right-sizing" Morningstar Wealth and the AssetMark TAMP transaction
value.stated_position: Management defines right-sizing as growing sustainably with margin improvement toward profitability; it announced AssetMark will acquire roughly $12 billion of assets on the Morningstar TAMP and that Morningstar planned to sunset its TAMP, with a negative short-term profitability impact and a positive run-rate impact after the 12-month transition.

investor_qa.quote: Subsequent to the annual shareholders meeting, we announced that AssetMark will be acquiring roughly $12 billion in assets administered on the Morningstar Turnkey Asset Management Platform (TAMP) and that we planned to sunset our TAMP.

value.topic: SMArtX minority investment and commercial relationship
value.stated_position: Management declines to comment on the operating performance of minority investments and says the commercial relationship with SMArtX is expected to wind down as accounts transition to the AssetMark platform.

investor_qa.quote: We do not comment on the operating performance of our minority investments. Morningstar’s commercial relationship with SMArtX is expected to wind down as we transition accounts from our platform to the AssetMark platform.

value.topic: Integration progress on the Praemium acquisition
value.stated_position: Management says the acquired U.K. and international business is performing well and helping drive underlying growth in Morningstar Wealth, listing milestones including full functional team integration, technology split from the parent with no downtime, launching Morningstar portfolios on the International Wealth Platform, merging fund ranges, cloud migration, and an enhanced retirement proposition.

investor_qa.quote: We have hit several key milestones since the acquisition of Praemium’s U.K. and international business, which is performing well and helping to drive underlying growth in our Morningstar Wealth segment.

value.topic: Product roadmap for Morningstar Indexes
value.stated_position: Management says it continues to focus on investable products and growing the benchmark data product, and that its near-to-midterm roadmap will leverage unique IP from the broader Morningstar enterprise, including differentiated private markets offerings through collaboration with PitchBook.

investor_qa.quote: We will continue to build on our strengths in these core areas while our near-to-midterm new product roadmap will continue to leverage the unique IP presented by the broader Morningstar enterprise including differentiated offerings in private markets through our collaboration with PitchBook.

value.topic: Differentiation of Morningstar Indexes versus S&P Global, MSCI and other incumbents
value.stated_position: Management points to combining indexing experience and independent global calculation capability with Morningstar's research, data and IP, and describes Morningstar Indexes as "a highly flexible challenger brand" better positioned to meet client needs and provide better value.

investor_qa.quote: Further, as a highly flexible challenger brand, we believe that Morningstar Indexes is often better positioned to meet the needs of financial service providers and their investors and provide better value to clients, as evidenced by our continued success in securing benchmark switches and new mandates.

value.topic: Rationale for floating- versus fixed-rate debt
value.stated_position: Management says the 2019 DBRS acquisition ($669 million total consideration) was funded with floating-rate debt to give prepayment and refinancing flexibility, that the strategy was successful given the 2020 $350 million private placement at a 2.32% coupon, that current mix is roughly 60% floating and 40% fixed, and it remains open to adding longer-term fixed-rate debt.

investor_qa.quote: Our current mix is roughly 60% floating and 40% fixed. While we value the flexibility to prepay without penalty offered by our bank debt, we remain open to future opportunities to add longer-term fixed-rate debt to the capital structure.

value.topic: Leverage policy and target
value.stated_position: Management states it has no leverage target but has always sought a strong balance sheet for capital allocation flexibility, notes the leverage ratio fell from 2.5x at March 31, 2023 to 1.4x at June 30, 2024, and says it remains open to increasing leverage if deemed the right thing to do to generate returns, within a 3.5x covenant.

investor_qa.quote: While we do not have a leverage target, we have always sought to maintain a strong balance sheet to allow for capital allocation flexibility. That has allowed us to invest in the business, be opportunistic with acquisitions (PitchBook, DBRS, and LCD), and return cash to shareholders.

value.topic: Why share repurchases have not restarted and dividend growth
value.stated_position: Management says buybacks and dividends are an important part of capital allocation strategy but the recent focus has been on paying down debt; the dividend was increased in 2024 from 37.5 cents to 40.5 cents per share, with roughly 9% CAGR over ten years.

investor_qa.quote: While both share repurchases and dividends are an important part of our capital allocation strategy (as noted in a related question this month), our recent focus has been on paying down debt. In 2024, we increased our dividend from 37.5 cents per share to 40.5 cents per share.

value.topic: Sale of Morningstar Commodity and Energy Data business to ZEMA Global Data Corporation
value.stated_position: Management said the business "was not material relative to the broader Data and Analytics segment," that associated revenue will be excluded from organic revenue growth calculations starting in Q4 2024, that the divestiture is expected to be "slightly dilutive to Data and Analytics margins," and that while they do not share transaction multiples, they "believe we achieved a positive result and unlocked value for a non-core business."

investor_qa.quote: While we do not share transaction multiples, we believe we achieved a positive result and unlocked value for a non-core business.

value.topic: Whether PitchBook competes with Hamilton Lane's Cobalt; market share
value.stated_position: Management views Cobalt as complementary to PitchBook, and although it lacks detailed market share data, believes PitchBook is the market leader in private market data based on the breadth and depth of its coverage.

investor_qa.quote: We view Hamilton Lane’s Cobalt product offering as complementary to PitchBook given their strengths in monitoring private market activity and commitment to providing transparency to asset owners. We do not have detailed market share data; however, we believe that PitchBook is the market leader in private market data based on the breadth and depth of our coverage.

value.topic: Independence of Sustainalytics ESG ratings and separation of analytical from commercial staff
value.stated_position: Morningstar Sustainalytics has developed a conflicts of interest framework and maintains a governance structure with clear reporting lines and separation of analytical and commercial activities, with personnel physically separated and using segregated IT systems and data subject to different access control protocols.

investor_qa.quote: More specifically, Morningstar Sustainalytics maintains a governance structure with clear reporting lines, roles, and responsibilities and separation of analytical and commercial activities.

value.topic: Data center energy use, AI scaling, and net zero goals
value.stated_position: The company is reducing its data center footprint to gain energy efficiencies in the public cloud, expects emissions to shift from scope 2 to scope 3, prioritizes cloud providers committed to net zero and renewable energy, and says scaling AI will require greater emphasis on data center energy efficiency and partner selection for both net zero goals and operational cost control.

investor_qa.quote: We are in the process of reducing our data center footprint which is expected to allow us to take advantage of meaningful energy efficiencies in the public cloud.

value.topic: Board independence and refreshment in light of ICGN independence criteria
value.stated_position: The Board believes independent directors should account for a substantial majority of the Board, but also that it is useful and appropriate to have key members of management, such as the Chairman and CEO, as directors; all standing committees are led by and composed entirely of independent directors, and the company evaluates skills and ongoing board refreshment annually.

investor_qa.quote: Morningstar’s Board of Directors believes that independent directors should account for a substantial majority of the Board, but also that it is useful and appropriate to have key members of management, such as our Chairman and our CEO, as directors.

value.topic: CFO transition and continuity of strategy
value.stated_position: Michael Holt, current Chief Strategy Officer and President of Research & Investments, was named CFO effective January 1, 2025, following "a rigorous selection process, which included interviews with internal and external candidates." Jason Dubinsky steps down at end of 2024 "to pursue other interests" and will consult through June 30, 2025. Management states: "We expect continuity in our strategy through the CFO transition. We will continue to focus on growing our adjusted operating income and free cash flow to increase shareholder value."

investor_qa.quote: We expect continuity in our strategy through the CFO transition. We will continue to focus on growing our adjusted operating income and free cash flow to increase shareholder value.

value.topic: Long-term capital allocation priorities, dividend versus buybacks
value.stated_position: Management restates four long-term priorities: preserve a strong balance sheet for flexibility; prioritize funding organic growth and consider acquisitions where they see opportunities to generate long-term shareholder value; maintain and increase the dividend commensurate with financial results; and repurchase shares when cash is available, accelerating "opportunistically when we believe that our shares are substantially undervalued." Given leverage at approximately 1.2x, they are "carefully assessing our best use of cash," one outcome being a 12.3% quarterly dividend increase from 40.5 to 45.5 cents for 2025.

investor_qa.quote: - We aim to maintain and increase our dividend over time commensurate with company financial results; and - We look to repurchase shares when we have available cash and will accelerate that activity opportunistically when we believe that our shares are substantially undervalued.

value.topic: Debt paydown following the LCD acquisition
value.stated_position: Management says the debt-financed 2022 LCD acquisition caused a substantial increase in leverage and that, with higher interest rates, "over the past 18 months we have been focused on paying down debt," with leverage down to approximately 1.2x as of September 30, 2024.

investor_qa.quote: With the 2022 acquisition of Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD), which we financed with debt, we saw a substantial increase in our leverage. As a result of that increase and higher interest rates, over the past 18 months we have been focused on paying down debt.

value.topic: Use of divestiture proceeds
value.stated_position: Management says that if it determines to use proceeds from the AssetMark transaction and the sale of the Commodity and Energy Data business to repay debt, leverage ratios could come down further — framed conditionally rather than as a commitment.

investor_qa.quote: If we determine to use the proceeds from the AssetMark transaction and the sale of our Commodity and Energy Data business to repay debt, you could see our leverage ratios come down further.

value.topic: Further divestitures of sub-scale or non-core businesses
value.stated_position: Management says it evaluates the product portfolio on an ongoing basis "to allocate investment to the best opportunities for widening our economic moat and driving long-term value creation," notes the completed Commodity and Energy data sale and the December 1, 2024 disposition of roughly $12 billion of TAMP assets to AssetMark, and states it plans to sunset the TAMP.

investor_qa.quote: On an ongoing basis, we evaluate our product portfolio to allocate investment to the best opportunities for widening our economic moat and driving long-term value creation.

value.topic: Margin expansion goal and headcount
value.stated_position: Management confirms the goal is annual adjusted operating margin returning to recent peaks "in the low 20 percent range" and higher, and states: "Over the long term, we are focused on increasing revenues at a faster rate than our adjusted operating expenses, with the goal of margin expansion and increasing free cash flow over time." It declines to share headcount projections.

investor_qa.quote: Over the long term, we are focused on increasing revenues at a faster rate than our adjusted operating expenses, with the goal of margin expansion and increasing free cash flow over time. We do not share headcount projections

value.topic: Competitive position in structured credit ratings
value.stated_position: Management concedes it does not have a significant CLO ratings business while its largest competitors are more active there, which has helped drive their growth; it says it continues to see opportunities in structured credit and "attractive prospects in private and middle market corporates in the U.S. and Europe."

investor_qa.quote: That said, we do not have a significant business in rating collateralized loan obligations, while our largest competitors are more active in this sector, which has helped drive their growth.

value.topic: Change in Advisor Workstation / App Hub partnership strategy
value.stated_position: Management says that based on learnings over the past 18 months it adjusted its App Hub strategy "to only partner with solutions that are closely connected to our core strategy and directly connected to the Advisor workflow," resulting in fewer partners going forward, and expects to deliver an upgraded Advisor Workstation in early 2025.

investor_qa.quote: Based on our learnings over the past 18 months, we've adjusted our strategy to only partner with solutions that are closely connected to our core strategy and directly connected to the Advisor workflow.

value.topic: Loss of a research distribution client to insourcing
value.stated_position: Management states the softness was largely driven by a client loss — a large global bank, a client since 2019 that sourced Morningstar equity research for buyside distribution — which "made the strategic decision to stop using third-party research and to bring all research in house." Research distribution was roughly 5% of Morningstar Data and Analytics revenue for the trailing 12 months.

investor_qa.quote: The client in question was a large global bank who had been with us since 2019 and sourced our equity research and distributed it to buyside clients. The client ultimately made the strategic decision to stop using third-party research and to bring all research in house.

value.topic: Sustainalytics strategy to return to growth and licensed ratings model change
value.stated_position: Management lists initiatives in climate (regulatory/reporting use cases, banking segment), broader data set improvements including CSRD support, and commitment to "strengthening our market-leading second party-opinion product." It notes a shift in the licensed ratings product away from a model under which corporate clients could contract for a rating, which has reduced revenue but "better positions us to scale that product over time."

investor_qa.quote: Finally, we’ve noted a shift in our licensed ratings product to focus on licensing existing ESG Risk Ratings as we’ve moved away from a model under which corporate clients could contract with us to provide a rating. The change in our product offering has led to a recent decline in revenue for the licensed ratings product in corporate solutions, but we believe it better positions us to scale that product over time.

value.topic: ESG competitive dynamics and vendor consolidation
value.stated_position: Management attributes the ESG slowdown to vendor consolidation as "many clients rationalized their ESG providers following a period of strong growth when they may have purchased multiple, overlapping ESG products," plus client focus on regulatory compliance over investment integration, and says competitors' strength in climate data and in indexes pressures its retention efforts.

investor_qa.quote: we have noted challenges in this space, and this has in turn also put pressure on our broader retention efforts with clients who have already selected one of our competitors to provide climate data. We believe that competitors are also able to leverage their strengths in other areas, including indexes, in support of their ESG products.

value.topic: PitchBook product roadmap
value.stated_position: Management says the roadmap reflects "a focus on expansion of data and research alongside product enhancements, including AI-driven tools," including private credit capabilities (BDCs and CLOs), non-backed company data, global databases and APAC research, private capital indexes with Morningstar Indexes, and expanded AI-driven document summaries.

investor_qa.quote: The PitchBook product roadmap continues to reflect a focus on expansion of data and research alongside product enhancements, including AI-driven tools.

value.topic: PitchBook management bonus plan terminated after CEO departure
value.stated_position: Management states the PitchBook management bonus plan "was designed primarily as a compensation vehicle for John" (former PitchBook CEO John Gabbert) and was terminated in Q3 24 following his departure, with stock forfeiture positively affecting PitchBook adjusted operating income.

investor_qa.quote: The plan was designed primarily as a compensation vehicle for John and was terminated in Q3 24.

value.topic: Japan strategy after terminating the Morningstar Japan licensing agreement
value.stated_position: Management says that with the termination completed "the Morningstar brand is in our full control," it now sells most products through a new subsidiary, Morningstar Japan, which "has helped eliminate the brand confusion that we previously faced," has hired a local manager research team, and is expanding beyond first-tier financial institutions to fintech startups and developing solutions for independent financial advisors.

investor_qa.quote: With the termination completed, the Morningstar brand is in our full control. We have moved to selling most products through a new subsidiary, Morningstar Japan, which has helped eliminate the brand confusion that we previously faced.

segments_basis.basis: reportable segments as named by the filing

investor_qa_basis.basis: management's written answers to questions submitted by investors, published roughly monthly. Same verification as every other fact — whole-document boundaries and a checked quote — but a different kind of evidence from a 10-K or proxy statement: unaudited, unprompted by any disclosure requirement, and responsive to whatever was asked. Corroborating; not a substitute for a filed disclosure.

ids.basis: content hash of the claim, its evidence and its source — see `fact_id` in src/ledger_schema.py. Confidence and the verification result are NOT hashed, so re-verifying a fact does not renumber it. Cross-year uniqueness is enforced fatally at build time by `audit_ids`.

corrections.basis: config/corrections.toml — human corrections to model-extracted values that the cited filing contradicts, each carrying the filing text that establishes it. data/ledger/facts/ is never edited: the record of what the model returned has to stay as it was.
